attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. David Kim, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden right groin pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns with acute worsening of a right groin bulge initially assessed by General Surgery on January 15, 2020. She reports a 3-month history of a bulge in the same region that would often appear with standing or coughing and spontaneously reduce. Today, however, the bulge became painful and could not be reduced. She denies nausea or vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Femoral hernia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Chronic constipation

Her medical history includes three vaginal deliveries and chronic constipation.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Spontaneous vaginal delivery x3

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Femoral hernia
- Father: Hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine weekly). Occupation: Part-time retail cashier.

VITAL SIGNS:
Vital signs are stable.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, she has a tender, non-reducible mass located inferior to the inguinal ligament and lateral to the pubic tubercle. The mass does not extend into the labia. Bowel sounds are absent over the mass.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Elena Rodriguez, MD
Department: General Surgery
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Bulge in right groin noticed several months ago

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She reports that the swelling is small and somewhat uncomfortable but not painful. It becomes more pronounced when she is standing or after prolonged periods of walking.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Chronic constipation

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
No prior abdominal or pelvic surgeries.

MEDICATIONS:
She takes no daily medications.

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Femoral hernia
- Father: Hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine weekly). Occupation: Part-time retail cashier.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
She has no nausea, vomiting, constipation, or abdominal pain. She denies trauma, fever, urinary symptoms, or recent illness.

VITAL SIGNS:
Vital signs are stable,

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, there is a small, firm, non-tender mass located just below the inguinal ligament on the right side. The bulge becomes more prominent with coughing and reduces with gentle pressure. No overlying skin changes.
and bowel sounds are present and normal.
